newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-New deals post impressive gains. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-New deals post impressive gains. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT]

text.p: Demand for initial public offerings looked strong on Wednesday, with three companies posting strong gains after their market debuts.

Boston Properties Inc rose seven percent, adding 1-3/4 to 26-3/4 in heavy trading, beating some analysts' expectations. It was the second most active issue on the Big Board at midday, with more than seven million shares traded.

The real estate investment trust (REIT), headed by Canadian-born real estate mogul Mortimer Zuckerman, sold 31.4 million shares for $25 (corrects from $26) each, the top of its estimated pricing range of $24 to $26.
Company founders Zuckerman and Edward Linde now own a 31.9 percent stake in Boston Properties, according to the prospectus. Zuckerman owns the New York Daily News newspaper.
Boston Properties will own 75 properties in New York, Boston and Washington when the offering is completed.

Aris Corp surged more than 25 percent after its IPO. Shares were up 3-7/8 to 18-7/8 at midday. The Seattle company provides computer training and consulting, primarily to companies that use Microsoft Corp and Oracle Corp software.
Aris sold two million of the 2,020,800 shares sold in the offering for $15 each, the high end of price talk of $13 to $15. About 21 percent of the company was sold to the public.
Company founder and chairman Paul Song and his wife, Tina, now own about 47.4 percent of Aris, which now has about 9.4 million shares outstanding.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Montgomery Securities and Piper Jaffray are underwriters.
Last year, the six-year-old company had net income of $2 million on revenues of $26.9 million, compared with income of $2 million and revenues of $14.8 million in 1995.

Colorado software company New Era of Networks Inc shares were up nearly 20 percent at midday, up 2-3/8 to 14-3/8. New Era sold 2.76 million shares for $12 each, the high end of its pricing range of $10 to $12. UBS Securities was the lead underwriter of the offering.
New Era filed in January for an IPO of 3.3 million shares but amended its registration in late May for an offering of 2.3 million shares.
All three deals priced at the high end of their initial public offering ranges. After the market close, a hot IPO is due to price from Morgan Stanley.

ARM Financial Group Inc, an asset manager, will sell eight million shares for $14 to $16 each, up from an earlier estimate of 5.75 million shares at $12 to $14 each. The shares are registered to trade on the American Stock Exchange under the symbol "ARM".
